summary: Enterprise AI model API aggregators have become the dominant way large organizations consume foundation models, offering a unified, governed layer over models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, Cohere, and others. These managed services keep data within the customer's cloud boundary, integrate with existing security and billing frameworks, and address the compliance requirements that prevent many enterprises from calling vendor APIs directly. Adoption is concentrated among hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, Google) that bundle model access with their broader cloud ecosystems.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy: prompts and completions stay within the company's cloud tenant/VPC and are not used to train vendor models, satisfying strict data governance rules.
Compliance and certifications: aggregators inherit the cloud provider's SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, FedRAMP, and GDPR attestations, reducing vendor-risk assessment overhead.
Single billing and consolidated contracts: model usage rolls into existing cloud commitments and committed-spend agreements, simplifying procurement and leveraging enterprise discounts.
Unified security and governance: integration with existing IAM, VPC networking, private endpoints, audit logging, and key management (KMS) applies consistent controls across all models.
Model choice and avoiding lock-in: access to multiple foundation models through one API lets teams switch or compare models without re-architecting integrations.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per 1K tokens plus Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved capacity; billed through Azure.
platforms.best_for: Enterprises standardized on Microsoft/Azure needing production-grade access to OpenAI models with strong compliance.

platforms.name: Amazon Bedrock
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token on-demand plus Provisioned Throughput for reserved capacity; batch discounts; billed through AWS.
platforms.best_for: AWS-centric enterprises wanting a broad multi-model marketplace with Anthropic and Llama alongside Amazon models.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token/character and per-request; Provisioned Throughput available; committed use discounts; billed through Google Cloud.
platforms.best_for: Data-heavy enterprises on Google Cloud/BigQuery wanting Gemini plus third-party models with strong MLOps tooling.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx.ai
platforms.pricing: Resource Unit (RU) token-based pricing plus subscription tiers; available on IBM Cloud, on-prem, and hybrid.
platforms.best_for: Regulated industries and hybrid-cloud enterprises prioritizing governance, explainability, and on-prem options.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based using Snowflake credits per token; billed within existing Snowflake account.
platforms.best_for: Enterprises running analytics on Snowflake wanting LLMs applied directly to governed data without ETL.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-character/token on-demand plus dedicated AI clusters for reserved capacity; billed through OCI.
platforms.best_for: Oracle-centric enterprises (ERP/database workloads) needing isolated, dedicated generative AI capacity.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token/neuron usage with generous free tier; billed through Cloudflare.
platforms.best_for: Developers and enterprises needing low-latency, globally distributed inference and a lightweight AI proxy layer.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs) per token/compute; billed within Databricks/underlying cloud.
platforms.best_for: Enterprises building custom models and RAG on the lakehouse with strong data governance and MLOps.

platforms.name: NVIDIA NIM / AI Enterprise
available_models: many optimized open models as microservices
platforms.pricing: Per-GPU subscription licensing (NVIDIA AI Enterprise); deployable on any cloud or on-prem.
platforms.best_for: Enterprises wanting maximum deployment control and GPU-optimized self-hosted inference across any environment.
